```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(broom)
library(afex)
library(nFactors)
library(plotrix)
library(effsize)
library(emmeans)
library(mediation)
library(apa)
library(multcomp)
library(gtools)
library(lavaan)
library(bwrappers)
# To install bwrappers, un-comment the following commands
#if(!require(devtools)){install.packages("devtools"); library(devtools)}
 #           install_github("michaelkardas/bwrappers")
```

```{r}
# Import data
col_names <- names(read_csv(here("data", "gender_study2_raw_data.csv")))
raw_data <- read_csv(here("data", "gender_study2_raw_data.csv"), 
                     col_names = col_names, skip = 3)
```

```{r}
# Filter out incomplete (or preview) responses, and rename some variables
# Note that a few participants took the survey after failing the attention check (and thus have an incomplete earlier response in the data), but there do not appear to be any instances of multiple complete responses from the same IP address
gender_data <- raw_data %>%
  filter(Finished == 1, Status == 0, !is.na(age), male != 2) %>%
  mutate(self_comp = (self_qualified + self_competent + self_skills + self_succeed) / 4,
         other_comp = (other_qualified + other_competent + other_skills + other_succeed) / 4,
         other_comp_5 = (other_qualified + other_competent + other_skills + other_succeed + other_likelihood) / 5,
         condition = factor(condition),
         choice_order = factor(Choice_order),
         DV_order = factor(DV_order),
         age_center = age - mean(age),
         race = factor(replace_na(race_wh5_5, 0)),
         # Note that the coding of gender in the survey is opposite to that of Study 1 (as shown below), but it will be recoded after this
         male = fct_recode(factor(male),
                           female = "0",
                           male = "1"),
         # Now I want to change which gender is the "reference group" so the results are consistent with Study 1 (men as reference group/0, female as 1)
         male = factor(male,
                       levels = c("male", "female")),
         # Create separate column for each pair of IVs combined
         condition_combined = factor(str_c(male, condition, sep = "_")),
         # Create dummy-coding of the three cells vs. the low experience females cell
         condition_dummy = as.numeric(fct_recode(condition_combined,
                                      `1` = "female_low",
                                      `0` = "female_high",
                                      `0` = "male_low",
                                      `0` = "male_high")) - 1) # subtracting one because converting to a numeric for some reason adds 1 to the values, making them 1 vs. 2, and 0 vs. 1 seems clearer
```


```{r}
# Functions

plot <- function(data, dv) {
data %>%
  group_by(male, condition) %>%
  summarize(count = n(),
            mean = mean(!!enquo(dv)),
            lower = mean(!!enquo(dv)) - std.error(!!enquo(dv)),
            upper = mean(!!enquo(dv)) + std.error(!!enquo(dv))) %>%
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = male, y = mean, fill = condition)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(1)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("lemonchiffon2", "mediumorchid")) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = .4, position = position_dodge(1)) +
    labs(x = "Participant Gender", fill = "Experience Condition") +
    theme_classic()
}

plot_paper <- function(data, dv) {
data %>%
  group_by(male, condition) %>%
  summarize(count = n(),
            mean = mean(!!enquo(dv)),
            lower = mean(!!enquo(dv)) - std.error(!!enquo(dv)),
            upper = mean(!!enquo(dv)) + std.error(!!enquo(dv))) %>%
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = male, y = mean, fill = condition)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(1), color = "black") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "gray30"),
                      # Note that in the code for the actual plot, the experience levels are recoded so low experience comes first
                      labels = c("Low", "High")) +
    # Note that in the code for the actual plot, the male/female levels are recoded so female comes first
    scale_x_discrete(labels = c("Female", "Male")) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = .4, position = position_dodge(1)) +
    labs(x = "Participant Gender", fill = "Experience Condition") +
    theme_classic()
}

table <- function(data, dv) {
  data %>%
    group_by(male, condition) %>%
    summarize(mean = round(mean(!!enquo(dv)),2),
              sd = round(sd(!!enquo(dv)),2))
}

table_contrast <- function(data, dv) {
  data %>%
    group_by(condition_dummy) %>%
    summarize(mean = round(mean(!!enquo(dv)),2),
              sd = round(sd(!!enquo(dv)),2))
}
```

# Alphas for Composites

## Self Measures

```{r}
psych::alpha(data.frame(gender_data$self_qualified, gender_data$self_competent, gender_data$self_skills,
                        gender_data$self_succeed))
```

## Other Measures (5-item)

```{r}
psych::alpha(data.frame(gender_data$other_qualified, gender_data$other_competent, gender_data$other_skills,
                        gender_data$other_succeed, gender_data$other_likelihood))
```

## Other Measures (4-item)

*Note that this does not include the fifth item, likelihood of colleagues voting. This 4-item composite is analyzed in the supplement.*

```{r}
psych::alpha(data.frame(gender_data$other_qualified, gender_data$other_competent, gender_data$other_skills,
                        gender_data$other_succeed))
```

# MAIN ANALYSES (for reporting)

## Choice Measures

### Likelihood of Running (Continuous)

```{r}
plot(gender_data, run_likelihood) +
  labs(y = "Mean Likelihood of Running")
```


```{r}
cts_likely_anova <- aov_car(run_likelihood ~ condition * male + Error(ResponseId), data = gender_data,  type = "III", 
                            anova_table = list(es = "pes"), include_aov = TRUE)
anova_apa(cts_likely_anova, print = FALSE) %>%
  kable(caption = "Regular ANOVA") 
```

```{r}
pairs(emmeans(cts_likely_anova, "condition", by = "male")) %>%
  kable(caption = "Pairwise Contrasts")
```

```{r}
pairs(emmeans(cts_likely_anova, "male", by = "condition")) %>%
  kable(caption = "Pairwise Contrasts")
```

```{r}
# Need lm object for effect sizes within the pairwise contrasts
likelihood_regression <- lm(run_likelihood ~ condition * male, data = gender_data)
eff_size(emmeans(likelihood_regression, "condition", by = "male"), 
                 sigma = sigma(likelihood_regression), 
               edf = df.residual(likelihood_regression)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Effect Sizes")
```

```{r}
# Need lm object for effect sizes within the pairwise contrasts
likelihood_regression <- lm(run_likelihood ~ condition * male, data = gender_data)
eff_size(emmeans(likelihood_regression, "male", by = "condition"), 
                 sigma = sigma(likelihood_regression), 
               edf = df.residual(likelihood_regression)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Effect Sizes")
```

```{r}
table(gender_data, run_likelihood) %>%
  kable(caption = "Means and SDs")
```

```{r}
gender_data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean = round(mean(run_likelihood),2),
                   sd = round(sd(run_likelihood),2)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Experience Condition Means")
```

**Analyses with contrast coding**

```{r}
wrap.t.ind(gender_data$run_likelihood, factor(gender_data$condition_dummy), var.equal = FALSE)
```


*Note that this was calculated by dummy-coding the female-low experience cell as 1, and all other cells as 0, and then running a t-test on this dummy variable.*


```{r}
table_contrast(gender_data, run_likelihood) %>%
  kable(caption = "Means and SDs")
```

### Choice to Run (Binary)

```{r}
# High and low experience total count

high_exper_female_count <- nrow(gender_data %>% filter(condition == "high", male == "female"))
low_exper_female_count <- nrow(gender_data %>% filter(condition == "low", male == "female"))
high_exper_male_count <- nrow(gender_data %>% filter(condition == "high", male == "male"))
low_exper_male_count <- nrow(gender_data %>% filter(condition == "low", male == "male"))

high_exper_female_table <- gender_data %>%
  filter(condition == "high", male == "female", choice == 1) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(count = n()) %>%
  mutate(proportion = count / high_exper_female_count,
         lower_bound = proportion - sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / high_exper_female_count),
         upper_bound = proportion + sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / high_exper_female_count),
         condition = factor("high"),
         male = "female")

low_exper_female_table <- gender_data %>%
  filter(condition == "low", male == "female", choice == 1) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(count = n()) %>%
  mutate(proportion = count / low_exper_female_count,
         lower_bound = proportion - sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / low_exper_female_count),
         upper_bound = proportion + sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / low_exper_female_count),
         condition = factor("low"),
         male = "female")

high_exper_male_table <- gender_data %>%
  filter(condition == "high", male == "male", choice == 1) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(count = n()) %>%
  mutate(proportion = count / high_exper_male_count,
         lower_bound = proportion - sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / high_exper_male_count),
         upper_bound = proportion + sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / high_exper_male_count),
         condition = factor("high"),
         male = "male")

low_exper_male_table <- gender_data %>%
  filter(condition == "low", male == "male", choice == 1) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(count = n()) %>%
  mutate(proportion = count / low_exper_male_count,
         lower_bound = proportion - sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / low_exper_male_count),
         upper_bound = proportion + sqrt(proportion * 
                                           (1 - proportion) / low_exper_male_count),
         condition = factor("low"),
         male = "male")

bind_rows(high_exper_female_table, low_exper_female_table, high_exper_male_table, low_exper_male_table) %>%
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = male, y = proportion, fill = condition)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(1)) +
  #scale_x_discrete(labels = c("")) +
  #scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("")) +
  geom_errorbar(mapping = aes(ymin = lower_bound, ymax = upper_bound), width = 0.4, position = position_dodge(1)) +
  labs(title = "Proportion Choosing to Run", y = "Proportion of Participants", x = "Participant Gender", 
       fill = "Experience Condition") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("lemonchiffon2", "mediumorchid")) +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r}
tidy(glm(factor(choice) ~ condition * male, data = gender_data, family = "binomial")) %>%
    mutate(signif = stars.pval(p.value)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Regular Logistic Regression")
```


```{r}
pairs(emmeans(glm(factor(choice) ~ condition * male, data = gender_data, family = "binomial"), 
               "condition", by = "male")) %>%
  kable(caption = "Pairwise Contrasts")
```

```{r}
pairs(emmeans(glm(factor(choice) ~ condition * male, data = gender_data, family = "binomial"), 
               "male", by = "condition")) %>%
  kable(caption = "Pairwise Contrasts")
```

```{r}
bind_rows(high_exper_female_table, low_exper_female_table, high_exper_male_table, low_exper_male_table) %>%
  kable(caption = "Proportions")
```

**Analyses with contrast coding**

```{r}
tidy(glm(factor(choice) ~ condition_dummy, data = gender_data, family = "binomial")) %>%
    mutate(signif = stars.pval(p.value)) %>%
  kable(caption = "Logistic Regression with Dummy Coding")
```


*Note that this was calculated by dummy-coding the female-low experience cell as 1, and all other cells as 0, and then running the regression on this dummy variable by itself.*


```{r}
gender_data %>%
  group_by(condition_dummy, choice) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  kable()
```

## Simultaneous Mediation with Contrast Codes (5-item other composite)

```{r}
multipleMediation <- '
choice ~ b1 * self_comp + b2 * other_comp_5 + c * condition_dummy
self_comp ~ a1 * condition_dummy
other_comp_5 ~ a2 * condition_dummy
indirect1 := a1 * b1
indirect2 := a2 * b2
total := c + (a1 * b1) + (a2 * b2)
self_comp ~~ other_comp_5
'
fit <- sem(model = multipleMediation, data = gender_data, se = "bootstrap",
           bootstrap = 5000)
summary(fit)
```

**Confidence intervals corresponding to the model above**

```{r}
parameterEstimates(fit,
                   boot.ci.type = "norm",
                   level = .95, ci = TRUE,
                   standardized = FALSE) %>%
  kable()
```

The second to last two rows above (before the total effect) contain the confidence interval estimates for each of the indirect effects.

## Plot to Report in Paper (Continuous Choice Measure)

```{r}
# Reordering the experience variable just for this graph, so it's presented more clearly
gender_data_relevel <- gender_data %>%
  mutate(condition = factor(condition,
                                 levels = c("low", "high")),
         # also recoding gender so that female goes first in the graph
         male = factor(male,
                       levels = c("female", "male")))

# The following code generates the plot in a separate PDF file (this was used for submission for the proofs)
#pdf("wald_figure4.pdf", width = 10, height = 7)

plot_paper(gender_data_relevel, run_likelihood) +
  labs(y = "Mean Likelihood of Running") +  
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 13),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 13))

#dev.off()
```

# Demographics

* *N* = `r nrow(gender_data)` (excluding non-binary genders)
* Mean age = `r round(mean(gender_data$age),2)`, SD age = `r round(sd(gender_data$age),2)`
*  `r length(gender_data$male[gender_data$male == "female"]) / nrow(gender_data)` female
*  `r length(gender_data$race_wh5_5[gender_data$race_wh5_5 != 1]) / nrow(gender_data)` non-White

# Balance Table for Demographics

## Condition N's

```{r}
gender_data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(count = n())
```

## Gender

```{r}
gender_data %>%
  group_by(condition, male) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(count = n())
```

```{r}
wrap.chi(gender_data$male, gender_data$condition)
```

## Race

```{r}
gender_data %>%
  group_by(condition, race_wh5_5) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(count = n())
```

```{r}
# Need to replace the NAs with 0's in order to conduct the chi-square test
wrap.chi(factor(ifelse(is.na(gender_data$race_wh5_5), 0, gender_data$race_wh5_5)), gender_data$condition)
```

## Age

```{r}
gender_data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_age = round(mean(age),2)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
wrap.t.ind(gender_data$age, gender_data$condition)
```
